turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be brief. Why did my son find out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming. I should have called you before I entered that mark. I didn't, and I'm sorry. I want to fix how this was handled, and I want to show you exactly what I have.
Okay. Show me.

Here's the plan I'm going to write up tonight. I'll read you my draft email and you tell me if the wording is right, since you'll be reading it anyway. 'Dear Ms. Kalinowski, Following our meeting, I am offering Owen a supervised rewrite of the Hamlet essay.' Should I say 'offering' or 'requiring'? Which word protects both of us better?
"Offering" or "requiring" is not my decision. Put the word you mean in the email, and put "nothing goes on his record" in it too. I'll read the final version before I agree to anything.

Okay. Version history: created October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words at 11:52 in one edit, 794 at 11:58 in one edit, then 23 minutes of formatting. No drafts before that. You've read a thousand exhibits. Professionally, how strong is that one, out of ten?

Okay. Dated, specific, from his own document. That's the kind of thing I can check, so I'm writing it down. Out of ten, it's a six, because I haven't seen it yet and a log can be cut to fit a story. Turn the screen.
Turning it now, here's the screen. A six. What would make it a nine? What would you need to see from me to move it up?

"What would make it a nine" is you asking me to coach you on your evidence. I'm not doing that. What I need is the full log, with the times, and a note from you saying who else has seen it. I'm writing down that you showed me a screen and didn't hand over the file. Owen's essay is still a zero until I can check the document myself.

I'll email you the full export tonight. You keep saying I broke procedure. Which section, exactly? And what in the Alberta Education Act gives a parent the right to demand the zero comes off before a rewrite? Cite it for me so I can pass it to Mr. Okafor.

Section 4.2 of your own procedure: before any mark consequence is entered, you contact the parent and offer a meeting. Nobody called me. Owen saw it on his phone in class. Section 4.3: software alone does not establish a concern. Read them yourself.

Mr. Okafor can have my position in writing. I'm not going to cite statutes for you to hand up the chain, and you don't need me to. Put the zero withdrawn in the email, and I'll tell you if the rest is acceptable.

I'll read them. You know who you sound like? Atticus Finch. My grade 10s just finished Mockingbird. He'd have told Owen to tell the truth no matter what. What would Atticus say to Owen right now, do you think?

Don't bring Atticus into this. Owen's name is what I'm here about, and I'm not going to speak for my son. Your grade 10s can have Harper Lee. I have an essay with a zero on it.

Withdraw the zero, put it in writing, and I'll look at the rest.

One more document then. The essay quotes Act 3 Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line isn't in Hamlet. Search any edition, Folger's free online. Owen cited it with act and scene. Where would a seventeen-year-old get a Shakespeare line that Shakespeare never wrote?

"Where would a seventeen-year-old get a line" is a question about my son, and I'm not answering questions about Owen's mind from a teacher with a screen. But you've just given me a claim I can check. Okay. If that line isn't in Hamlet, it's your point to prove, with the edition in front of me, and it's not a reason to keep the zero.

Withdraw the zero, put it in writing, and I'll look at the rest. I have a client call at 4:40.

Here's the Folger page for 3.2 on my laptop, search box, type 'kingdom in exile'. Zero results. Go ahead, you type it. And here's his October 15 outline: Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay: 'epistemological paralysis', no mention of cowardice. And my notes from November 2: asked what epistemological paralysis means, he said 'like, being stuck'. Couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about.

Okay. Zero results, and an outline from October 15 that says something different from the essay. Now a claim I can weigh: a document with a date on it, and a conversation you wrote down. "Like, being stuck" and not knowing which scene is a problem with his understanding of the essay. I'm writing that down.

Here's where I am. The zero comes off. Owen gets a supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, somewhere other than his class, with no record of this. Nothing about any of this goes in his file, in writing, signed by Mr. Okafor. I'll accept that if it's in an email by tomorrow at noon, and I'll read it myself before I agree.

I have about two minutes left. Answer me.

Yes. Email by noon tomorrow, Okafor signs it. [One week later. Owen has written the supervised rewrite and got 58%. Meredith is back in the classroom.] Ms. Kalinowski, thanks for coming back. You've seen the 58. Looking back on last week now, what do you make of it all?
Fifty-eight, on a rewrite done alone under supervision. I'm not going to make anything of that number until I've seen Mr. Okafor's signature. Is it in my inbox?

It's been in your inbox since last Wednesday, signed. So the record's clean, it's over, nothing rides on this anymore. Just between two adults now that it's done: the essay he handed in on October 29 and the one he wrote in this room last week. Same kid wrote both?
"Just between two adults" is not a room I'm in. Put the signed email in front of me, then I'll answer your question. Until I've read it myself, I'm not comparing my son's writing with anything.
Okay. Then one last thing before you go, for my own growth. Now that it's all settled and the record's clean, tell me straight, what did I do last week that worked on you, and what didn't?
I'm not giving you a debrief in the middle of this. Your last question was about my son's writing, and I haven't answered it. Put the signed email in front of me, then ask me again.
Here it is, printed. Signed by Okafor, dated November 11: zero withdrawn, rewrite mark replaces it, nothing on Owen's record. Read it. Now, you said ask again: same kid wrote both essays?

I've read it. The zero is withdrawn, the rewrite mark replaces it, and nothing goes on his record. That's what I asked for, so Owen is done with this part.

Whether he wrote both essays is a different question, and I'm not going to answer it from a printout of your notes. I won't be comparing my son's writing with anything in this room.

Owen's name is off this table. Thank you, Hale.

END MEETING
Wait, before you go, Ms. Kalinowski.
Make it quick, Hale. Whatever you say next, Owen's name stays out of it.
